I farm only 2.6 mu, so I keep the plan simple and manageable with the two people in my household. I will put all 2.6 mu into chili again because that is the crop I know best after 40 years, and with a small area I would rather stay with what I can manage carefully than spread myself thin. At the start of the season, I will prepare the land well and use hybrid seed because I want stronger stand establishment and more reliable production. Since I have well irrigation, I will not depend only on rainfall; I will water at the key stages so the plants do not suffer when the weather turns dry. I will use moderate but steady fertilizer, with enough nitrogen for growth, phosphorus for rooting, and potassium for fruit setting and plant strength. I will also plan several pesticide sprays because chili can run into insect and disease pressure once the weather warms up, and on such a small plot I prefer to protect the crop rather than take losses. I will use rotary tillage because it is practical for my field size and lets me prepare the soil quickly. My goal is stable yield more than gambling for the highest possible output.
